channel.title: Lean Weekly
channel.description: News about Lean, the theorem prover and programming language.

item.title: Lean v4.36.0 released with type class resolution caching across commands
item.description:
The cross-command cache cuts type class resolution time on the standard library build by about 14% (Mathlib gains 0.2% overall). Other changes fix many grind bugs and several quadratic slowdowns (on a file with 4,000 definition/theorem pairs, elaboration time drops from 99 s to 32 s), and let def contracts state exception postconditions.

Sources: v4.36.0 release notes, lean4 v4.36.0

item.title: Harmonic's Aristotle now formally verifies Rust, joining C and Verilog
item.description:
Harmonic says users can prove that Rust code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its specification says, even if it uses unsafe, and that Rust code ported from C behaves the same as the original. The Lean account on X welcomed the use of Lean for Rust verification.

Sources: @HarmonicMath on X, @leanprover on X

item.title: Nockchain releases a Nock zkVM with an end-to-end Lean soundness proof
item.description:
The Open Proof Machine's verifier checks a short proof instead of re-running a program in Nock, a tiny combinator language; kernel-checked soundness and completeness theorems cover all twelve opcodes, unbounded natural-number atoms and jets (known formulas that an interpreter replaces with native code). The alpha research release has not been independently audited.

Sources: nockchain.org, nockchain/nock-zkvm

item.title: Harmonic's Lean-powered Aristotle adds Rust verification alongside C and Verilog
item.description:
Aristotle can prove that Rust code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its spec says, even inside unsafe blocks (code the compiler does not check), and that C rewritten in Rust matches the original. On Manifest, an open-source Solana order book, Aristotle proved 28 results and found a rounding bug, since fixed.

Sources: harmonic.fun, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: OKcontract Labs releases Zean for proving Zig functions in Lean
item.description:
The open-source toolkit translates supported Zig functions into executable Lean models, working from Zig's analyzed intermediate representation (AIR); an included copy-loop example proves its model avoids invalid accesses and uninitialized reads. Lean checks the translated model under its stated assumptions, so the proofs do not establish correctness of the final native binary.

Sources: okcontract.com

item.title: Aaron Elijah Mars verifies 15 Ethereum tokens' deployed bytecode in Lean 4
item.description:
The proofs, 7,024 theorems in total, cover every input, caller and order of calls for tokens worth about $54 billion on Ethereum, including DAI, UNI, SHIB and PEPE. They show balances always add up to the total supply (or supply grows only as the rules say) and who can mint, freeze, blacklist or pause.

Sources: aaronjmars/proven-tokens

item.title: NyxFoundation publishes LeanAsm, a Lean 4 foundation for verified RV64 assembly
item.description:
LeanAsm covers typed RV64IM (RISC-V) and scalar x86-64 assembly, executable machine semantics, encoding, and source emission; it is intended to be shared by ssz-asm, cl-asm, and p2p-asm. Its architecture follows the verified macro-assembly approach demonstrated by Verified-zkEVM's evm-asm while remaining independent of EVM, zkVM execution, and riscv-zkvm.

Sources: NyxFoundation/LeanAsm

item.title: Logan R. Chalmers lowers four-dimensional Borsuk bound to six, formalized in Lean
item.description:
Logan R. Chalmers proves that every set of diameter one in four dimensions can be split into at most six parts of smaller diameter, improving the previous upper bound of seven; five are sometimes necessary. The proof uses cones, balls or a rational polytope depending on circumradius, and the theorem is formalized in Lean.

Sources: arXiv:2611.17375

item.title: Mark Lewko formalizes sharp Kakeya bounds in every dimension, with AI assistance
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry proves two upper estimates, on the Kakeya maximal operator (largest averages over tubes around unit segments in each direction) and weighted tube overlaps, and says they imply the Kakeya maximal function conjecture. Only those two estimates are Lean theorems, and the repository discloses the lack of independent human mathematical review.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, mrklwk/kakeya-sharp

item.title: Juan Pablo Traverso Gianini directs AI to formalize Peter Keevash's triangle-decomposition theorem
item.description:
Written by Harmonic's Aristotle and Claude Opus 5.5, the Lean proof of Theorem 2.1 of "Counting designs" assumes typicality on every set of at most 16 vertices, stronger than the paper's pairs-only hypothesis, so the paper's version is not covered. The proof replaces the Completion stage's random greedy algorithms with a deterministic potential argument.

Sources: jtraverso/keevash-triangle-decompositions, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Nethermind's Foxglove formalizes a separation logic for probabilistic programs in Lean
item.description:
Built on iris-lean, Foxglove adapts the Bluebell logic of Bao, D'Osualdo and Farzan to functional programs and is intended to support verifying cryptographic primitives formalized in ArkLib. Every rule of the logic is proved against a semantic model with no axioms beyond Lean's own, and the Ethereum Foundation funded the work.

Sources: NethermindEth/Foxglove, reservoir.lean-lang.org

item.title: Scidonia Limited ports libexpat's XML 1.0 parsing semantics to Lean 4
item.description:
The port, lexpat, is aimed at untrusted input and has a resumable streaming core, machine-checked properties of its UTF-8 decoder, and a bounded differential fixture against libexpat. A C header and shared library for x86_64-linux provide a subset of libexpat's XML_* calls; namespace processing, DTDs and external entities are not implemented.

Sources: scidonia/lexpat, reservoir.lean-lang.org

item.title: emberian's qsag combines post-quantum threshold signing in Rust with Lean proofs
item.description:
The research-preview stack implements NIST FIPS 205 SLH-DSA-SHAKE and FIPS 204 ML-DSA-44, and Lean certificate checks pass for its 19 x86-64 and 9 AArch64 certified assembly kernels. Its main-library axiom audit checks 59,257 declarations, including 28,744 kernel theorem declarations, across 57 modules, with no rejected axioms.

Sources: emberian/qsag

item.title: Claude and Codex agents produce complete Lean formalization of restricted isometry paper
item.description:
The paper, by Christian Kümmerle and Dustin G. Mixon, constructs explicit restricted isometries (measurement matrices for compressed sensing) beyond the square-root barrier believed to limit its proof technique. The agents, directed by the authors, proved every numbered result, including the needed case of Zahl's sphere-tangency theorem, but no running-time bound.

Sources: ckuemmerle/ExplicitRIPTwoThirds, arXiv:2611.14475, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Lexifina formalizes the US tax code in Lean, finding 138 drafting mistakes
item.description:
Lexifina used AI to translate each section of the tax law into Lean, staying close to the statute's own words, and tested it against worked examples in IRS forms and instructions. Each drafting mistake has a Lean certificate proving the fault, and a comparison with three tax programs found bugs in Tax-Calculator and UsTaxes.

Sources: lexifina.com

item.title: Mahdi JafariRaviz formalizes Robertson and Seymour's Graph Minors series in Lean 4
item.description:
The formalization covers all 838 numbered results across 22 papers, including the graph minor theorem (Wagner's conjecture), the excluded-minor structure theorem, and the O(n³) algorithm for the k disjoint paths problem. The three main theorems pass comparator and use only the standard axioms; the repository describes corrections to the papers, none affecting those theorems.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Grothendieck Labs publishes a Lean formalization of Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch
item.description:
The proof covers projective morphisms of smooth quasi-projective varieties over a field, uses no sorry and no axioms beyond Lean's standard three, and rests on Stacks for Chow groups and Chern classes. It was made on the grothendieck platform with the model Fable 5.2 in 6 hours 23 minutes.

Sources: grothendiecklabs/grothendieck-riemann-roch

item.title: Malvin Gattinger answers an open logic question using LLMs and Lean
item.description:
Malvin Gattinger's arXiv paper gives a counterexample showing that test-free PDL (Propositional Dynamic Logic without the '?' operator) lacks Craig Interpolation, which Borzechowski et al. (2026) showed PDL has. The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean, and the paper links to all prompts, LLM output summaries and the Lean proof.

Sources: arXiv:2611.16759, doi.org

item.title: Igor Inozemtsev registers Lean proof of Ben Green's Problem 64 in Palomar
item.description:
The proof shows, without additional hypotheses, that there are infinitely many primes p for which p minus 2 has an odd number of prime factors, counted with multiplicity. The standalone development, credited to gpt-6 astra and adapting Jizhou Guo's argument, includes supporting analytic number theory and uses Mathlib as its only direct Lake dependency.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, inozemtsev/formal-math, data.palomar-registry.org

item.title: okcontract publishes Solidity Spec, an executable formal model of Solidity in Lean
item.description:
The Lean 4.29.0 package targets Solidity 0.8.36 and comes with a paper on its semantics and trust boundary. Conformance checks compare selected executions with the pinned compiler and a local Cancun EVM; okcontract calls the formalization incomplete and notes that compiler compatibility, scoped to viaIR: true, is not a proof of general compiler conformance.

Sources: okcontract/solidity-spec

item.title: mathematics-inc runs Linux's WireGuard handshake code in Lean, finding undefined behaviour
item.description:
The repository holds the Cerberus Core of a program running a complete two-peer WireGuard handshake, as readable Lean modules with one definition per WireGuard C function. Running it under a C semantics in Cerberus-Lean produced output identical to an independent reference implementation and also found limitations of Cerberus and Cerberus-Lean.

Sources: mathematics-inc/wireguard-handshake-cerberus-lean

item.title: Leo de Moura is guest speaker at an NYU Courant seminar
item.description:
NYU Courant announced in a November 13 post on X that Leo de Moura would speak at a special Mathematics in the Age of AI Seminar the next day at 3:30pm in Warren Weaver Hall. The post links to more information on NYU Courant's website.

Sources: @NYU_Courant on X

item.title: AxiomMath publishes AI-written Lean formalization of Faltings' theorem, the Mordell conjecture
item.description:
The library, about 430 modules written by AI agents, follows E. Bombieri's proof, builds on Mathlib and the Stacks Project in Lean, and proves the statement of the LeanEval faltings problem verbatim. Lean's kernel checks every proof, with no sorry, no native_decide, and no added axiom; humans have not yet reviewed the code.

Sources: AxiomMath/Mordell

item.title: Dave Goel proves in Lean that Smale's mean value constant equals 4
item.description:
S. Smale proved in 1981 that this constant, defined from the critical points of complex polynomials, is at most 4 and asked whether 4 can be replaced by 1. A 2026 Lean disproof by T. Adamczewski ruled out 1, and Dave Goel's proof shows no constant smaller than 4 works for all degrees.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, david44hello/paper_smale-mean-value-constant-equals-4

item.title: Cătălin I. Cârstea and Lauri Oksanen formalize anisotropic Calderón uniqueness in Lean
item.description:
The proof covers a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calderón uniqueness theorem OpenAI released on October 6, 2026 without a Lean proof: three-dimensional unit ball, full boundary measurements, metrics Euclidean outside the ball. It builds on Mathlib and the Tau Ceti analytic library and answers a comparator challenge permitting only Lean's standard axioms.

Sources: arXiv:2611.10537, catalin-carstea/anisotropic-calderon-lean

item.title: Salvatore Mercuri and Bhavik Mehta formally verify Riemann hypothesis up to 10⁸
item.description:
Lean's kernel checks, using only the standard axioms, that the first 248,008,818 nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line. The announcement calls this the first kernel-checked verification at this scale; the build of more than 6 million modules took over 240,000 CPU hours on EPCC's Cirrus supercomputer.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com, smmercuri/zeta, zenodo.org

item.title: Axiom formalizes first seven chapters of Introduction to Cluster Algebras in Lean
item.description:
Using Axiom's AxiomCode tooling, AI agents (Anthropic's Claude) formalized 1,348 of 1,429 blueprint entries, one per definition or result, from the textbook by Sergey Fomin, Lauren Williams, and Andrei Zelevinsky. The Mathlib-based library declares no axioms, stating its 31 assumptions as explicit hypotheses, and Lean's comparator checks that it proves eleven headline theorems.

Sources: axiommath.ai, clusteralgebras.axiommath.ai, AxiomMath/ClusterAlgebras

item.title: Bartosz Naskręcki publishes Lean Doom Lab, pairing Doom play with Lean proofs
item.description:
Users can play a route, pause on a game tick and inspect its Lean proof; in a browser course of nine authored maps, all 27 supplied route witnesses have stock Lean kernel audits. The lab's first-safe-exit theorems state that the player remains alive, physics succeeds and the last input raises the exit flag.

Sources: nasqret/leandoom-proofs

item.title: Kamil Braun's Kotlean runs proven Lean code inside Android apps
item.description:
Developers write an app's state, behavior and UI in Lean, prove properties of that code, and compile it into the app, while a small Kotlin host renders native Android Views. Examples include SnackNet, an original maze-chase game written in Lean, and Counter, a smaller starter with buttons and an editable note.

Sources: kbr-/kotlean

item.title: Peter Burton formalizes a group whose nontrivial Bernoulli shifts are all isomorphic
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry covers all standard probability bases whose measures are not point masses, with possibly different or infinite entropies. The countable group is built from the group of an OpenAI construction, which supplies the algebraic existence input; the formalization does not certify finitary or continuous conjugacy and says nothing about other groups.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, peterburton1728/bernoulli-iso-1

item.title: yang-mills-group posts OpenAI construction of pure Yang-Mills in Lean
item.description:
The construction, obtained October 28, 2026, proves a challenge statement with a Mathlib-only import closure: for each closed matrix subgroup with nonabelian simple real Lie algebra, a Wilson lattice family with a Wightman reconstruction (positive energy, unique vacuum). A kernel replay found only standard axioms; a positive mass gap is outside the challenge's scope.

Sources: yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028

item.title: Crowd-sourced project aims to make the 4D Yang-Mills Lean proof human-readable
item.description:
The hairer/humanise-yang-mills repository plans a research monograph giving detailed proofs, traceable to a fixed version of the announced Lean formalisation of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory, with contributors' agents working on tasks claimed through GitHub issues. Preliminary dependency mapping is under way; a full build, axiom audit, and line-by-line mathematical audit are still outstanding.

Sources: hairer/humanise-yang-mills

item.title: With LongTails, AI agents prove more than 100 new Lean-verified optimization bounds
item.description:
In the Lean 4 framework by Alexander Tyurin, QuocViet Pham, Valentin Khrulkov, and Ivan Oseledets, agents such as Codex or Claude Code search for better oracle-call budgets under a fixed problem setup, and Comparator independently audits each result. One new gradient-only guarantee for (L0,L1)-smooth convex optimization resolves what the authors call an open problem.

Sources: arXiv:2611.13872, k3nfalt/longtails

item.title: Christian Merten and collaborators formalize the Weil conjectures with AI assistance
item.description:
AI agents (Anthropic Claude models) wrote most of the proof under the authors' supervision, and the team spent about 80,000 USD on model access and server compute. The Lean proof certifies the conjectures as stated in LeanEval; a blueprint website presents it as layered natural-language notes, unfinished in parts not directly needed for it.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com, formal-arithmetic-geometry/weil-conjectures, weil-conjectures.merten.dev, axiommath.ai

item.title: Physical Superintelligence releases an AI-produced Lean proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
item.description:
The conjecture says a bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. AI models produced the proof, paper and formalization in a research harness developed by David Turturean at PSI; the formalization has no placeholder or added axiom and was re-checked by two independent Lean kernel implementations.

Sources: physical-superintelligence/aaronson-ambainis

item.title: ChatGPT Pro and Claude Opus 5.5 prove the Reinhardt conjecture in Lean
item.description:
The conjecture, open since 1934, says the smoothed octagon (a regular octagon with its corners cut off by hyperbola arcs) packs the plane worst among centrally symmetric convex shapes. The-Anh Vu-Le directed the work, which follows Thomas Hales's optimal control formulation; no person has checked the proof, though Lean's kernel checks every step.

Sources: vltanh/lean4-smoothed-octagon, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Axiom Math formalizes all four Weil conjectures in Lean
item.description:
The library, Weil, has about 220,000 lines of code, written by AI agents and not yet reviewed by humans; reusing Axiom Math's earlier Lean formalization of the Stacks Project, an algebraic geometry reference, let the team finish in 24 hours. The top-level theorem copies verbatim the LeanEval problem weil_conjectures, which uses only Mathlib definitions.

Sources: axiommath.ai, AxiomMath/Weil, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Antony Lewis proves the Higuchi-Sudbery entanglement conjecture, with a Lean formalization
item.description:
Among four-qubit pure states, only M₄ and its complex conjugate, up to local unitaries, maximize the mean von Neumann entropy of the three balanced bipartitions; the paper also proves the Gour-Wallach conjecture for Rényi entropies. The Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization covers most four-qubit results and parts of the computer-assisted seven-qubit ones.

Sources: arXiv:2611.05757, cmbant/qubit-entropy

item.title: Murali Menon proves Herzog-Schönheim conjecture for solvable groups, with Lean formalization
item.description:
The Herzog-Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. The arXiv paper proves it for all solvable groups, finite or infinite, and the proof has been formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

Sources: arXiv:2611.11002

item.title: Carlos Toledo formalizes a seven-point counterexample to Graham's spherical-set conjecture
item.description:
Dömötör Pálvölgyi's heptagon and generic seven points on a circle (Theorem A.3 of arXiv:2609.23327) are proved non-Ramsey under formal-conjectures' definition, copied byte for byte (Ramsey: for any number of colours, every colouring of some Euclidean space has a monochromatic copy). Anthropic's Claude wrote the Lean proofs under Carlos Toledo's direction, building on OpenAI's formalization.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, carlostoledo1891/heptagon-ramsey-lean

item.title: The-Anh Vu-Le registers Lean proofs of Brouwer's, Kakutani's and Schauder's fixed-point theorems
item.description:
Brouwer's theorem, in every finite dimension, has two proofs: an analytic one, following John Milnor (1978) and C. A. Rogers (1980) and using no homology, degree theory or simplicial approximation, and one through Sperner's lemma. Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the proofs in Claude Code; no person has reviewed them, and Lean has checked them.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, vltanh/lean4-fixed-point

item.title: Veil 2.0 released for verifying distributed protocols in Lean 4
item.description:
The release adds verified model checkers for safety (2 to 20 times faster than TLC) and liveness, an LTL proof mode, a TLA+-to-Veil LLM skill, and a PlusCal-style DSL. George Pîrlea says Veil now supports anything the TLA+ Toolbox is used for; Ilya Sergey credits @zqy1018 and external contributors.

Sources: @ilyasergey on X, @GeorgePirlea on X

item.title: AI-written Lean model of CPython 3.15.2 finds hundreds of bugs
item.description:
David Andrews and Chao Zhang's model spans 613,318 lines of Lean with 18,898 theorems and lemmas; each modelled function must agree with the real interpreter on at least 50,000 cases. Of 26,004 functions in scope, 4,071 (15.7%) are judged faithful by independent review, and 418 bug records reproduce on 3.15.2, each with a reproducer.

Sources: Broyojo/python-formalization

item.title: Yalu Cai, Tung-Che Chang, and Santosh Nagarakatte verify an eBPF proof checker
item.description:
Keel, an in-kernel proof checker for the Linux eBPF verifier, is specified in Lean and proved sound against bit-vector semantics; its implementation in EmbC, a deeply embedded C fragment, is proved to refine that specification. Formalizing the eBPF Certificate Framework (BCF) checker uncovered 13 bugs, and Keel runs 1.3X faster than BCF's checker.

Sources: arXiv:2611.11117

item.title: Giulio rebuffo's usdt-verify formally verifies deployed USDT bytecode in Lean 4
item.description:
Built on EthLib's EVM model and program logic, the proofs are about the 11,075 deployed bytes read from Ethereum mainnet; the Solidity source served only as a guide. The README says each of its claims is proved and has passed several independent reviews, and that this does not mean USDT is verified unconditionally.

Sources: Giulio2002/usdt-verify

item.title: zkSecurity publishes Rust BLS12-381 code proved equivalent to the EthLib Lean specification
item.description:
The code covers field arithmetic, G1 encoding and decoding, and subgroup and pairing-product checks, specializing routines from the arkworks 0.5.0 crate; proofs establish termination and agreement with EthLib under documented preconditions, while arkworks agreement is tested and the Charon/Aeneas translation remains trusted. The project was mostly AI-generated and has not been independently reviewed.

Sources: zksecurity/arkworks-ethlib

item.title: Rudi Cilibrasi publishes openverse, an unofficial Verse runtime with Lean verification
item.description:
The project defines and proves the semantics of Verse (Epic Games' functional logic programming language) in Lean 4 and checks a C runtime against it. Its C components for integer arithmetic, program loading, and rollback are proved with QuickProof (VST and CompCert in Coq); differential testing and fuzzing check the object store and value heap.

Sources: rudi-cilibrasi/openverse

item.title: Markus de Medeiros publishes SampLib, a Lean library of verified random samplers
item.description:
SampLib expresses samplers from Peter Occil's articles as executable ProbLang terms and proves them correct in continuous TotalEris, building on logsem/clutch-lean and Lean 4.35.0. Its completed baseline suite contains 216 samplers, and the README notes that the interpreter tests are not proofs and that the interpreter uses finite-precision Float arithmetic.

Sources: markusdemedeiros/SampLib

item.title: yaneurao publishes Lean 4 proofs for a shogi AI opening-book algorithm
item.description:
The algorithm, peta-shock conversion, propagates evaluation values recorded in a shogi AI's opening book backward from the end positions and covers books containing ordinary and perpetual-check repetitions. PaperClaims.lean links the accompanying paper's theorem numbers to Lean theorem names, and Audit.lean checks the axioms the theorems depend on.

Sources: yaneurao/peta-shock

item.title: Andreas Andreakis extends DBLog to delete orphan rows, with Lean 4 proofs
item.description:
DBLog-based incremental snapshots, adopted by Debezium and Flink CDC, originally did not handle orphan rows (in the sink, absent at the source); the extension deletes keys a chunk read did not return. Safety and convergence are proved in Isabelle/HOL and, except for the Flink CDC theory, in Lean 4, with no unfinished proofs.

Sources: arXiv:2611.10810, doi.org
